issues: When user is in 'All Illakas' mode (selectedIllaka=null), the Add Entry modal shows all fields but illakaId is null. On submit, 'Please fill all fields' toast fires, but the user has filled all visible fields - there's no illaka dropdown in the modal. This is confusing UX. Fix: Either add an illaka dropdown to the entry modal when in All Illakas mode, OR disable/hide the Add Entry button when no specific illaka is selected.

action_items: UX improvement (not blocking): When admin is in 'All Illakas' mode and clicks Add Entry, the modal fails with generic 'Please fill all fields' error because illakaId is null. Add either: (a) an illaka selector in the entry modal when illakaId is null, or (b) disable the Add Entry button when no specific illaka is selected with a tooltip 'Please select an Illaka first'.
critical_code_review_comments: MINOR: AccountsModule.jsx lines 88-95: Uses `localStorage.getItem('token')` for Bearer auth in fetch calls, but AuthContext uses cookie-based auth (set_cookie on login). Since both frontend and backend are same-origin (same domain), cookies ARE sent by default with fetch(), so this works correctly. However, `Authorization: Bearer null` header is sent unnecessarily. Consider removing the localStorage token logic and relying on cookie-based auth only, or use `credentials: 'include'` in fetch options for cross-domain safety.
MINOR: Entry modal requires illakaId but has no illaka field - silent 'Please fill all fields' error when in All Illakas mode is confusing UX.
OK: Freeze check logic in /api/accounts/entries/expense uses date_type.today() which is server date (March 2026), correctly blocking past months for muneem.
OK: System heads (is_system=True) protected from deletion and deactivation at both API and UI levels.
OK: Double-entry bookkeeping correctly creates 2 balanced lines for both expense (Dr:Expense Cr:Cash) and income (Dr:Cash Cr:Income) entries.
OK: Sipahi access control is properly enforced: no sidebar link, redirected from /accounts route, 403 on write API calls.
OK: Cash Book balance calculation is correct: closing = opening + receipts - payments.
